title: Cocycle of the canonical fixed-point stalk transports
statement:
Use the global finite-field and finite-coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k$ its fixed algebraic closure, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ with $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, $X_0$ separated of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\Phi:X\to X$ be the $k$-linear $q$-power scheme Frobenius and $g=g_\gamma$ the geometric Galois-Frobenius automorphism [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use the derived module pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and put $Q_j=L(\Phi^j)^*$ and $P_j=L(g^j)^*$ for $j\geq1$. Fix a $k$-morphism $z:s\to X$ and a positive integer $d$ with $\Phi^d z=z$. Write $J_z(L)=L_z=R\Gamma(s_{\mathrm{proet}},Lz^*L)$ for the ordinary derived geometric stalk [pur9-def-derived-stalk], for $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

For each positive multiple $j$ of $d$, let $\rho_{j,L}:J_z(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_z(Q_jL)$ be the canonical composition comparison $L(\Phi^jz)^*\cong Lz^*Q_j$, followed by derived sections, with its source identified using $\Phi^jz=z$. The composition comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], with canonical constant-coefficient identifications. Using the specified multiplicative natural isomorphism $\kappa^{(j)}:Q_j\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], put
$$t_{j,L}=J_z(\kappa^{(j)}_L)\circ\rho_{j,L}:J_z(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_z(P_jL).$$
Then $t_j$ is natural in $L$: for every morphism $u:L\to M$,
$$J_z(P_j u)\circ t_{j,L}=t_{j,M}\circ J_z(u).$$
For positive multiples $a,b$ of $d$, let $c_{a,b}:P_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_aP_b$ be the canonical pullback-composition comparison (using $g^{a+b}=g^b\circ g^a$). Then
$$J_z(c_{a,b,L})\circ t_{a+b,L}=t_{a,P_bL}\circ t_{b,L}.$$
No Weil structure on $L$, closed point below $z$, trace, or perfectness hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Step 1: the composite identification for m=rd is the r-fold iteration of the one for d; naturality of the canonical stalk identifications

proof.text:
Write $J=J_z$ and $S=R\Gamma(s_{\mathrm{proet}},-)$. If $j=rd$ with $r\geq1$, induction gives $\Phi^{rd}z=z$: the base is the hypothesis and $\Phi^{(r+1)d}z=\Phi^{rd}(\Phi^dz)=\Phi^{rd}z$. By [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition], the canonical constant ring identifications used here agree with the composite ones required by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Thus $\rho_{j,L}=S(c_{z,\Phi^j,L})$, with $L(\Phi^jz)^*L=Lz^*L$ identified by the displayed equality. This is an isomorphism, and naturality of the cited functor isomorphism gives
$$J(Q_ju)\circ\rho_{j,L}=\rho_{j,M}\circ J(u).$$
Here $J=S\circ Lz^*$ is exactly the functor in [pur9-def-derived-stalk]; applying a functor preserves the naturality equality.

source.place: Step 1: functoriality and naturality of the fixed-point identifications; explicit agent calculation

proof.text:
By [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], $\kappa^{(j)}$ is a natural isomorphism on the ordinary derived category. Its coefficient hypothesis holds because $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, which is invertible in $k$. Applying $J$ to its naturality equation and then using Step 1 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
J(P_ju)\circ t_{j,L}
&=J(P_ju)\circ J(\kappa^{(j)}_L)\circ\rho_{j,L}\\
&=J(\kappa^{(j)}_M)\circ J(Q_ju)\circ\rho_{j,L}\\
&=J(\kappa^{(j)}_M)\circ\rho_{j,M}\circ J(u)
=t_{j,M}\circ J(u).
\end{aligned}$$
Each $t_{j,L}$ is an isomorphism since its two factors are isomorphisms.

source.place: Step 1: functoriality and naturality of the fixed-point identifications; explicit agent calculation

proof.text:
Let $e_{a,b}:Q_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_aQ_b$ denote $c_{\Phi^a,\Phi^b}$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence] with $j=z:s\to X$, $h=\Phi^a:X\to X$, $k=\Phi^b:X\to X$ and $M=L$. Its equality reads
$$Lz^*(e_{a,b,L})\circ c_{z,\Phi^{a+b},L}=c_{z,\Phi^a,Q_bL}\circ c_{\Phi^az,\Phi^b,L}.$$
The constant coefficient normalization is precisely the one in that cited statement. Since $a,b,a+b$ are positive multiples of $d$, Step 1 identifies $\Phi^az=z$, $\Phi^bz=z$ and $\Phi^{a+b}z=z$. In particular $c_{\Phi^az,\Phi^b,L}=c_{z,\Phi^b,L}$ after substitution. Apply the functor $S$ to obtain
$$J(e_{a,b,L})\circ\rho_{a+b,L}=\rho_{a,Q_bL}\circ\rho_{b,L}.$$
The cited lemma is for the unbounded derived categories and for arbitrary scheme morphisms, so it applies also to the geometric point $z$.

source.place: Step 1: functoriality and naturality of the fixed-point identifications; explicit agent calculation

proof.text:
Write $\kappa_r=\kappa^{(r)}$. Multiplicativity of the specified family in [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], with the composition comparisons displayed, means
$$c_{a,b,L}\circ\kappa_{a+b,L}=\kappa_{a,P_bL}\circ Q_a(\kappa_{b,L})\circ e_{a,b,L}.$$
Equivalently one may write $P_a(\kappa_{b,L})\circ\kappa_{a,Q_bL}$ on the right before $e_{a,b,L}$; the two expressions are equal by naturality of $\kappa_a$ for the arrow $\kappa_{b,L}:Q_bL\to P_bL$. Hence Step 3 and Step 1's naturality for that same arrow give
$$\begin{aligned}
J(c_{a,b,L})\circ t_{a+b,L}
&=J(\kappa_{a,P_bL})\circ J(Q_a(\kappa_{b,L}))\circ J(e_{a,b,L})\circ\rho_{a+b,L}\\
&=J(\kappa_{a,P_bL})\circ J(Q_a(\kappa_{b,L}))\circ\rho_{a,Q_bL}\circ\rho_{b,L}\\
&=J(\kappa_{a,P_bL})\circ\rho_{a,P_bL}\circ J(\kappa_{b,L})\circ\rho_{b,L}\\
&=t_{a,P_bL}\circ t_{b,L}.
\end{aligned}$$
Only functoriality, naturality and composition of isomorphisms are used after the cited multiplicative law. All arrows are in $D(A)$ after applying $J$; there is no Weil map, trace or finiteness condition on $L$.

split_report.summary: Expanded the fixed-point transports into canonical pullback comparisons. Naturality and the cocycle follow by the explicit triple-composition identity for (z, Phi^a, Phi^b), then multiplicativity and naturality of kappa. Reused existing coherence and constant-coefficient lemmas; no new nodes, no statement changes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes Step 1 of lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula: naturality of the canonical stalk identifications and the assertion that the identification for rd is the r-fold iteration for d.

Provides the triple-composition equation specialized to (z, Phi^a, Phi^b); a generic coherence tool, not a replacement trace argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N1-abf73a685 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all the mathematics in full and made no fixes. The statement is unchanged and every type checks; c_{a,b}: L(g^b g^a)^* -> P_aP_b follows the composition lemma's c_{h,k} convention. The hypotheses meet the cited nodes: A=O_E/varpi^n is finite and killed by a power of ell, which is invertible in k; k is algebraically closed, as pur9 needs; ell is invertible on X and on s. Step 1: lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition supplies the composite coefficient identification the composition lemma assumes. rho_j is S(c_{z,Phi^j}) with Phi^j z=z an equality of morphisms. J=S∘Lz^* is exactly pur9's definition, and its pullback is the same pbc-operations pullback. Step 2: kappa^{(j)} is natural on the unbounded D(X_proet,A); the chase is correct. Step 3: I re-derived lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence with j=z, h=Phi^a, k=Phi^b. The factors are e_{a,b}, c_{z,Phi^{a+b}}, c_{z,Phi^a}(Q_bL), and c_{Phi^a z,Phi^b}=c_{z,Phi^b}, which give the rho-cocycle after S. Step 4: the prop states only 'multiplicative iterate'. Its proof (Step 8) and blueprint_update give kappa^{(m+n)}=G_m(kappa^{(n)})∘kappa^{(m)}_{T_n} under the composition comparisons. That is the item's second form, and it equals the first by naturality of kappa_a. The four-line chain checks, using rho_a naturality at kappa_{b,L}. Source: main-20261015 lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula.proof.md Step 1, and Stacks 0D6D (sites-cohomology.tex l.3657, K-flat proof). Small cases tested: X_0=Spec F_q (Phi=id, reduces to kappa multiplicativity), a=b=d, a=d with b=2d, L=0, X empty, nonreduced X_0, and z not over a closed point. There are no new nodes and no duplicate: lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization is a single-m identity and lem-trf-frobenius-pullback-comparison-coherence concerns only g. There is no cycle, proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and nothing cites SGA. Accepted tool_uses: lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence, and prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison (named by the ancestor). Observation for the parent: def-trf-frobenius-operators defines the stalk as Fib_s(Lx^*M), while this item uses RΓ(s,Lz^*). The parent's claim t_{j,K}=tau_{z_j,j} implicitly identifies the two; that is not a fault of this delivery.
